newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Countrywide raises first half profit.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Countrywide raises first half profit.

text.p: Countrywide Bank on Thursday reported a tax-paid profit of NZ$28 million for the first half to August 31 against $21.4 million a year earlier.
Countrywide, a unit of Bank of Scotland, said its profit before tax was up 33 percent at NZ$44 million.
Total operating income rose 12.8 percent to NZ$113 million.
Managing Director David Wolfenden said New Zealand's competitive banking environment continued to pressure the bank's core areas - residential mortgages and retail banking.

Adding to this was the political uncertainty of the country's first elections under proportional representation, which had brought continuing speculation and doubt about interest rates and the exchange rate.
Total customer deposits showed strong growth, increasing by NZ$441 million in the past six months.
Operating expenses were largely controlled, rising by just 2.7 percent to NZ$69 million and bringing the expenses/income ratio down to 61 percent from 68 percent.
Residential lending grew to NZ$382 million from $352 million, giving Countrywide 11 percent of the market.
Wolfenden said the bank intended to continue expanding on its strategy of using "mobile mortgage managers" -- staff who visit customers and potential customers in their homes.
The strong first half was due to Countrywide's policy of exploiting niche opportunities, particularly in business and small business banking, with mobile managers being a key part.
Other highlights were the launch of Capital Equipment Finance Ltd and the opening of a Hong Kong subsidiary to service the bank's Asian Banking Division.
Wolfenden said he anticipated a continued good performance from the bank in the second half - from both its core businesses and its growing niche markets.
